essence: All opposites shine in the consciousness-mirror: true/untrue, little/much, eternal/non-eternal, Māyā-stained/self-pure. To know all things as light-natured, arising from one's own grasping consciousness, is the glory born of experience — Lordhood; worship is its final imperative. Knowing that all opposites shine in the mirror from one's own grasping consciousness = glory = Lordhood; its last word is the imperative it opened with the stance for.

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of Lordhood (viśveśvaratva); the vyabhicāri is wonder (camatkāra) at all opposites shining in the mirror from one's own grasping consciousness. The rasa is the tranquility of Lordhood — the hymn that began in anupāya ends in worship.
